whatIs: Joi is a JavaScript library for describing data schemas and validating them. It defines rules with a chainable API, comes with more than 150 built-in validators, and supports references between fields, dependencies and custom types through extensions. You install it with npm install joi.
It's a good fit when you need to validate the input of an API, a form or a configuration file in detail, especially in Node projects with rules that depend on other fields.
uses: Validating the body and parameters of an API's requests in Node before processing them.
Checking that a configuration file or the environment variables have the expected shape at startup.
Enforcing cross-field rules, such as requiring a field only if another one has a certain value.
caveats: It's a runtime validation library: it doesn't generate TypeScript types on its own, so if you want to infer them you may prefer another option.
The current version requires Node 20 or later.
The full documentation and the changelog are at joi.dev; the repository's README only links there.
pricingNote: Open source under the BSD 3-Clause license.
idealFor: Node backends that need to validate data with expressive rules.
